title: McKinney-Vento protections for homeless students
facts: The federal McKinney-Vento Act provides educational rights for children and youth experiencing homelessness in public schools.

Covered students can have rights involving immediate enrollment even when normally required records are unavailable, school stability, transportation in qualifying circumstances and access to comparable services.
The statutory definition can include children sharing housing because of loss of housing or economic hardship and children living in motels, shelters, cars or other inadequate temporary settings.
Local educational agencies must designate a liaison for students experiencing homelessness.
